display_name: The Evidence Act 1893 organised by evidentiary question: relevancy of facts, admissions and hearsay, records and opinions, character, proof of documents, presumptions and burden, witnesses and privilege, examination and credibility, bankers' books, with the conclusions it hands the Criminal Procedure Code
scope: The Evidence Act 1893 as printed in SSO's PDF, current version as at 01 Oct 2026: ss 2 to 33 and 34 to 176 (Parts 1 to 4) and the First and Second Schedules, except ss 117 to 119 (estoppel), which are NOT encoded. Inert (read, adding no condition or answer of their own): ss 1, 2(2), 3(6), 3(7), 31, 36A, 80B, 137, 140(1) and (4), 141, 142, 152, 156, 168, 175, 176, 177 and the rule-making powers (ss 32(4), 36A, 116A(5), 154A(2)), whose content is in other instruments. The restrictions of s 154A are a named REFUSE. Repealed: ss 24 to 30, 35, 36, 115. The Part 5 power to amend the Schedules is not applied: the Schedules are encoded as printed on 01 Oct 2026. NOTES.md section 2 gives each row.

not_reviewed.note: No domain expert has read this against the statute. An independent test pass was run on 2026-10-01 (tests-independent.l4, 954 assertions): it found three encoding errors, now fixed, and two assertions are left failing on purpose (forks F15 and F16). Its author read the modules for names and signatures, so it is not a substitute for expert review. The other assertions were written by the encoder from the Act's text and illustrations, in the same session as the rules. The source is SSO's unofficial consolidation. NOTES.md sections 7 and 9.

forks.F1: s 3(3) to (5): a set of facts that makes a fact both proved and disproved is a REFUSE, not a default.
forks.F2: s 8(2) Explanation 2: a statement made to or in the presence of a person whose conduct is relevant is relevant on its own, without being itself 'conduct'.
forks.F3: s 32(1)(b): the four things after 'in particular' are illustrations of the general limb, not further conditions.
forks.F4: s 33 Explanation: a criminal trial or inquiry is deemed to be between the prosecutor and the accused, so the 'same parties' condition is met where both proceedings are criminal between the same prosecutor and accused.
forks.F5: s 45A(2): the three exceptions (pending appeal, quashed, pardoned) are applied to a conviction, not to an acquittal.
forks.F6: s 83: the condition 'kept substantially in the form required by law and produced from proper custody' attaches to the second class (documents directed by law to be kept) only, not to the Gazette, newspaper or journal.
forks.F7: ss 109 and 110: where a person was shown alive within 30 years and has not been heard of for 7 years, s 110's 'shifted' burden governs.
forks.F8: ss 70 and 71: a document required to be attested may be used if no attesting witness can be found only on the proof s 71 describes; that no witness is alive is not itself enough.
forks.F9: s 32B(1)(2): a statement of opinion is relevant under s 32(1) only if it would be admissible as direct oral evidence.
forks.F10: s 122(5) is split: the Evidence Act and 'any other written law' limbs are facts here; the Criminal Procedure Code's ss 265 and 266 arrive as a field of the Code Conclusions interface record.
